text: The Patriots' 35-6 loss to Jacksonville on Sunday was an unmitigated disaster that has everyone—most importantly Drake Maye himself—questioning whether the offense is being deployed to his strengths, as the second-year quarterback coughed up three turnovers (two interceptions and a fumble) in what he called an "unacceptable" performance from both himself and the unit as a whole. Lawrence carved up New England's defense with three touchdown passes while Jaguars coach Liam Coen's team responded exactly as advertised after a week spent emphasizing accountability, leaving Mike Vrabel with plenty to unpack in Monday's press conference and raising the uncomfortable possibility that the Patriots' offensive scheme simply isn't maximizing their young signal-caller's talents. On the bright side, Marcus Jones recorded his first interception of the season in a game that offered precious little else to celebrate, making what should have been a learning moment feel more like a crisis of confidence and scheme fit for an organization that can't afford many more performances this lopsided.
